fieldMarks: Body feathers grey-black with white speckles; 51-64 cm, 1.1-1.8 kg; about 22 in in Hawaii
Bare head with sky-blue to dark-blue skin, a bony casque (larger in males) and wattles (smaller in females)
Juveniles: less developed casque and wattles, paler face, grey-brown overall; chicks have longitudinal head stripes
behavior: Terrestrial flocks roost in trees at night; flocks of one pair up to 100 birds, largest in winter
Runs from danger and flies only as a last resort, steeply upward
Harsh dry calls carry far; male gives a single 'chek', female a two-note 'buck-wheat'
Omnivorous: seeds, grain, bulbs, roots, fruit, snails, beetles, ticks, small lizards; dust bathes daily
habitat: Exposed areas with some trees for roosting: grassland, savanna, cultivated land and scrub, often near water; avoids dense forest, desert and marsh.
range: Native across most of sub-Saharan Africa. In Hawaii, domestic-type birds have been released and live in open urban fields near ponds and wetlands.
